newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India remains under pressure.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India remains under pressure.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) came under renewed pressure as the local market fell over two percent.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed down 0.89 points, 1.46 percent, at 60.18 points, with the premium over the local market at 8.41 percent compared with yesterday's 7.26 percent.
"Although most scrip was weaker, there was some demand for one or two stocks, but not much," said a trader.

The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index lost 66.96 points, or 2.07 percent, to 3,172.98, with ITC the main loser, down 18.25 rupees, or 5.68 percent, to 303 rupees on news of the arrest of senior company officials for allegedly breaking laws on export deals.
"ITC is a continual nightmare, the company is fined and then its executives get arrested," said the trader.
Elsewhere, Grasim was healthier, up 63 cents at $13.50/$14.50, but most other blue chips were weaker, with TELCO down 52 cents at $11.50/$12.50 and Reliance off 20 cents at $10.25/$11.25.
Overall Indian GDRs are down more than 20 percent this year and more than five percent during the past three months.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended off 1.03 points, 1.58 percent, at 64.31, a premium of 27.78 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index fell 13.76 points to a provisional 766.32.

The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended up 0.80 points, 0.92 percent, at 86.94, a premium of 1.64 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index shed 65.05 points, 1.01 percent, to 6,359.67. -- David Chance London newsroom 44 171 542 5887
